{
  "concerns": [
    {
      "id": "SKP-001",
      "concern": "Scope is enormous: 7 independent skills + 5 cross-cutting infrastructure libraries + Ed25519 signing + hash chains + trust store with offline root + jailbreak CI suite + machine fingerprinting, all in 6-10 weeks",
      "severity": "CRITICAL",
      "severity_score": 950,
      "why_matters": "Each of these subsystems alone (e.g., a signed audit log with key rotation/revocation/recovery) is typically a multi-month project. Sprint 1 alone bundles audit envelope + JCS + Ed25519 + trust store + offline root signing + protected class router + operator identity + tier validator + L1 panel skill. Historical software patterns suggest this slips by 2-3x. The 'Sprint 4.5 buffer week' is wildly inadequate. R11 acknowledges this but mitigations are aspirational (de-scope triggers, weekly check-ins) rather than structural.",
      "location": "Section 8: Development Phases; R11",
      "recommendation": "Hard cut scope: ship L1+L6+L7 with a minimal HMAC-chain (no Ed25519, no trust store, no offline root) as v1; defer L2-L5 and full signing infrastructure to a v2 cycle. Or extend timeline to 16-20 weeks honestly."
    },
    {
      "id": "SKP-002",
      "concern": "Offline root key for trust-store creates a single human bottleneck with no documented succession or availability SLA",
      "severity": "CRITICAL",
      "severity_score": 880,
      "why_matters": "§1.9.3.1 says 'maintainer offline → cannot sign updates → freeze new key issuance until next maintainer window.' If the maintainer is unavailable (vacation, illness, departure, lost YubiKey), no one can rotate keys, onboard operators, or respond to compromise. A compromised key during maintainer absence becomes catastrophic. There is no M-of-N threshold scheme, no documented succession, no break-glass procedure. The pinned root pubkey at .claude/data/maintainer-root-pubkey.txt is itself in a git-writable file, only protected by 'reviewer-only edits' which is a social control, not cryptographic.",
      "location": "§1.9.3.1 Trust-store root of trust",
      "recommendation": "Use M-of-N threshold signatures (e.g., 2-of-3 maintainers) or document explicit break-glass procedure with time-bounded recovery. Cryptographically pin root pubkey via signed release artifact, not a git-mutable file."
    },
    {
      "id": "SKP-003",
      "concern": "Hash-chain recovery via git history is fundamentally unsound for files that are explicitly UNTRACKED",
      "severity": "CRITICAL",
      "severity_score": 850,
      "why_matters": "§3.4.4 says recovery walks `git log -p <log_file>` to rebuild broken chains. But §3.7 declares .run/panel-decisions.jsonl, .run/cost-budget-events.jsonl, etc. as UNTRACKED. There is no git history for these files. The 'mandatory weekly snapshot' creates a 7-day RPO during which a chain break is unrecoverable. Worse, if an attacker tampers with the live log between snapshots, the snapshot itself may not detect the gap because the snapshot is just a copy of the current (possibly tampered) state. The recovery procedure is inconsistent with the persistence policy.",
      "location": "§3.4.4 vs §3.7",
      "recommendation": "Either track all chain-integrity-critical logs in git (with the operational pain that entails) or replace git-based recovery with append-only durable storage + offsite mirror. Reconcile §3.4.4 with §3.7 before implementation."
    },
    {
      "id": "SKP-004",
      "concern": "Tool-call boundary defense (Layer 5, §1.9.3.2) depends on heuristics that will misfire and block legitimate work",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "severity_score": 780,
      "why_matters": "'Heuristic: any tool call within first N turns where SessionStart content was present' will trigger constantly because SessionStart content is present at every session start by definition. This means every Bash/Edit/Write in the first N turns of every session will require 're-confirmation,' destroying the autonomous-operation value proposition (the whole point of the cycle per UC-1). Operators will either disable the check or build muscle memory to click through, defeating the security goal.",
      "location": "§1.9.3.2 Layer 5",
      "recommendation": "Define provenance more precisely: only tool calls whose arguments derive from SessionStart-tagged content should be denied/reconfirmed, not all tool calls in early turns. This requires data-flow tracking which is significantly harder than the SDD acknowledges."
    },
    {
      "id": "SKP-005",
      "concern": "Machine fingerprint based on hostname + MAC + machine-id is unstable and will produce false positives",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "severity_score": 720,
      "why_matters": "MAC addresses change (USB ethernet, Wi-Fi vs ethernet, randomized MACs on modern OS, VPN interfaces). machine-id can be regenerated on OS reinstall or container rebuild. Hostnames change. Every false fingerprint mismatch refuses audit-log writes (per §1.7.1), halting work and requiring `/loa machine-fingerprint regenerate`. In a developer environment with laptop sleep/wake, dock attach/detach, VPN toggle, this will trigger frequently. Operators will alias the regenerate command and stop reading reasons.",
      "location": "§1.7.1 Hard Runtime Guardrails",
      "recommendation": "Choose a single stable fingerprint source (e.g., persistent UUID written once) or accept that single-machine constraint is an honor-system policy r
